answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Malignant melanoma is defined by asymmetry, uniform cytologic atypia, and lack of maturation with depth [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180).
- Breslow thickness, mitotic rate, and ulceration are the most critical prognosticators [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html).
- Major subtypes include superficial spreading, nodular, lentigo maligna, acral lentiginous, desmoplastic, and nevoid variants [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticWHO.html).
- S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A are typically positive melanocytic markers [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html).
- Classic stromal features include dermal melanophages and a dense, bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate in most invasive lesions [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180).

## Terminology

- Malignant melanoma: malignant neoplasm derived from melanocytes in the skin.
- "Invasive melanoma": melanomas showing dermal (vertical) invasion, distinct from melanoma in situ.
- Synonyms (not recommended): malignant melanoma NOS, cutaneous melanoma.
- Includes subtypes: superficial spreading, nodular, lentigo maligna, acral lentiginous, desmoplastic, nevoid, and others [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticWHO.html).
- "NOS": used when further subtyping is not possible.
  
## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**  
  - Architectural and cytologic asymmetry [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html), [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180)
  - Poor circumscription/lack of sharp lateral borders [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html)
  - Lack of maturation with depth: deep melanocytes resemble superficial ones
  - Uniform cytologic atypia: large, hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, abundant cytoplasm [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180)
  - Pagetoid (upward) scatter of melanocytes into the epidermis (except in desmoplastic, pure nodular, or lentigo maligna types)
  - Increased dermal mitotic activity, especially if deep/atypical [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html)
  - Dermal/vertical invasion of neoplastic melanocytes
  - Breslow thickness: measured from the granular layer or ulcer base to deepest tumor cell [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1081)
  - Ulceration and mitotic rate (per mm²) are essential for staging and risk stratification
  - Stromal features: dermal melanophages and dense, bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate usually present [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180)
- **Desirable:**  
  - Identification of an in situ (radial growth phase) component at lesion edge
  - Immunohistochemistry profiling (S100, SOX10, Melan-A, HMB45) in difficult cases [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html)
  - Molecular confirmation may be helpful in diagnostically challenging or ambiguous cases (especially for metastasis, not required for most primary cutaneous cases) [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html)
  - Identification of molecular alterations supportive of melanoma (e.g., BRAF, NRAS)

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- Primary risk is UV exposure (intermittent and cumulative sun damage)
- Genetic driver mutations differ by pathway/subtype:
  - Low-CSD/superficial spreading: BRAF V600E most common [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html), [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180)
  - High-CSD/lentigo maligna: less frequent BRAF, NF1 and others
  - Acral/mucosal/desmoplastic: more KIT, NRAS, and additional mutational events [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html)
  - Aggressive forms may have TERT promoter, PTEN, or other mutations/deletions
- High nevus count increases melanoma risk [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnevigeneral.html)

## Clinical Issues

- **Epidemiology:**  
  - Most arise de novo, some within dysplastic nevi [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1215)
  - Wide age range; nodular type is common in older adults [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html)
  - Slight male predominance in several populations
- **Site:**  
  - Classic: trunk, lower leg, upper back, BANS sites (upper back, posterior arms/necks/scalp) [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1238)
  - Head/neck more often high-CSD (lentigo maligna); acral/subungual possible
- **Presentation:**  
  - Early: flat, pigmented asymmetric macule
  - Late: nodular, ulcerated/polychromatic mass; >6 mm size, irregular/scalloped border, color variegation, recent change, irritation or bleeding [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1238)
- **Natural History:**  
  - Most progress from radial (in situ) to vertical (invasive/dermal) phase; nodular forms may lack radial component
- **Prognosis:**  
  - Breslow thickness = most important marker [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html)
  - Ulceration, high mitotic rate, lymphovascular/perineural invasion, and sentinel node positivity are adverse features
  - Tumors on BANS sites can have a worse prognosis [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1238)
- **Treatment:**  
  - Surgical excision with negative margins is standard
  - Sentinel lymph node biopsy for staging
  - Systemic therapy based on mutations (BRAF/KIT inhibitors, etc.) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnevoidmelanoma.html)

## Macroscopic

- Asymmetric, variegated color (tan, brown, black, red, or amelanotic)
- Irregular, scalloped borders [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1238)
- Typical size >6 mm flags possible early melanoma
- Advanced lesions may be nodular/ulcerated

- Figures representative of major subtypes:
  - ![Superficial spreading melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati01.jpg)
  - ![Nodular melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati003.jpg)
  - ![Desmoplastic melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati06.jpg)
  - ![Lentigo maligna melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati05.jpg)
  - ![Acral lentiginous melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati32.jpg)

## Microscopic

- Defined by dermal (vertical) invasion of malignant melanocytes
- **Cellular features:**
  - Large, hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, abundant cytoplasm [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180)
  - Variable melanin; may be absent (amelanotic)
  - Uniform cytological atypia (not random as in dysplastic nevus)
- **Architectural features:**
  - Asymmetric, poorly circumscribed lesion
  - Absence of maturation with depth
  - Pagetoid (upward/suprabasal) scatter often present (less so in nodular/desmoplastic/lentigo maligna)
- **Mitoses:**  
  - Deep/atypical mitotic figures frequent; mitotic index is key [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html)
- Ulceration may be present
- **Stroma:**  
  - Dermal melanophages and a dense, bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate usually present in invasive lesions [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180)
- **Growth patterns:**  
  - Radial (in situ): contiguous atypical melanocytes along basal layer, +/- pagetoid upward spread
  - Vertical (invasive): nests/sheets of malignant melanocytes in dermis
- **Subtype-specific:**
  - Nodular: early vertical growth, little/no radial, poor circumscription, frequent ulceration
  - Lentigo maligna melanoma: crowded atypical basal melanocytes, variable pagetoid scatter, fibrosis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticlentigomaligna.html)
  - Desmoplastic: spindle cells in collagenous stroma, often non-pigmented, mimics scar [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticdesmoplasticmelanoma.html)

## Ancillary Tests

- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - S100: positive (sensitive, not specific)
  - SOX10: positive
  - Melan-A (MART-1): positive
  - HMB45: positive, except often negative in desmoplastic subtype [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html)
  - Dermal melanomas consistently express these markers [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html)
- **Molecular/genetics:**  
  - BRAF V600E most common in low-CSD (superficial spreading), and some nevoid melanomas [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html)
  - NRAS, KIT, TERT promoter, PTEN, NF1 — frequency varies with subtype
  - Molecular confirmation can be desirable in challenging cases [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html)
- **Cytology:**  
  - Uniform atypia with large, hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli
  - Lesional cells may show abundant melanin or be amelanotic

## Differential Diagnosis

- **Dysplastic nevus:**  
  - Random (not uniform) cytologic atypia; exhibits maturation with depth  
  - Lesional mitoses rare; lacks diffuse pagetoid spread  
  - Smaller, symmetrical, well-circumscribed margins [Textbooks](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=158)
- **Recurrent nevus:**  
  - Irregular scarring, lentiginous melanocytic hyperplasia; lacks deep invasion and uniform atypia  
  - May mimic melanoma (\"pseudomelanoma\") but lacks essential invasive features [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Recurrent_Naevus.html)
- **Sclerosing naevus:**  
  - Appears in the differential of recurrent nevus and melanoma [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Recurrent_Naevus.html)
  - Deep dermal sclerosis, small bland melanocytes, lacks atypical mitoses or expansile growth of melanoma
- **Dysplastic nevus with florid fibroplasia:**  
  - Also distinguished from melanoma by deep fibroplasia, lack of deep invasion, and no uniform cytologic atypia [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Recurrent_Naevus.html)
- **Nevoid melanoma:**  
  - Subtle pleomorphism, can mimic intradermal or congenital nevus  
  - Lacks true maturation, features expansile aggregates of atypical melanocytes, and expresses melanoma molecular markers [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnevoidmelanoma.html)
- **Desmoplastic melanoma:**  
  - Mimics scar or benign fibrous proliferation  
  - Spindle cell morphology, SOX10/S100 positive, HMB45 negative [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticdesmoplasticmelanoma.html)
- **Halo nevus with lichenoid inflammation:**  
  - Halo nevus: lichenoid interface reaction with no intraepidermal melanocytic proliferation of concern
    - Melanoma suggested by: a separate expansile cell population, severe cytologic atypia, frequent mitoses, ulceration, or necrosis [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Halo_Naevus.html)

- **Note:** Criteria for metastatic melanoma (e.g., a prior melanoma, subcutis-based nodule, molecular confirmation) are not applicable for primary invasive cutaneous melanoma [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).

cards.title: Halo naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Halo naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis of involuting halo naevi includes other lichenoid interface reactions, such as those seen in lichenoid keratosis and melanoma with lichenoid inflammation. Findings suggestive of melanoma include the presence of a separate population of cells with an expansile pattern of growth; severe cytological atypia; and frequent mitoses, ulceration, or tumour necrosis. The halo phenomenon may occasionally involve other types of naevi, including dysplastic, Spitz, and congenital naevi, as well as melanomas. In most lesions, there is no intraepidermal melanocytic proliferation adjacent to the dermal component. If in situ or superficially invasive melanoma is present adjacent to a dermal lesion simulating halo naevus, the entire lesion is most likely melanoma.

cards.title: Recurrent naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Recurrent naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis includes melanoma, dysplastic naevus, sclerosing naevus, and dysplastic naevus with florid fibroplasia.

cards.title: Mucosal melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucosal melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis includes dysplastic naevi and special-site naevi (see section Dysplastic naevus, and section Special-site naevi (of the breast, axilla, scalp, and ear)).

cards.title: Melanoma metastatic to the skin
cards.excerpt: Entity: Melanoma metastatic to the skin Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis of metastatic melanoma in the skin includes primary melanoma, primary dermal melanoma, and atypical naevus. Blue naevus–like metastases are difficult to distinguish from common or epithelioid blue naevus. The presence of cytologically atypical epithelioid melanocytes and mitotic figures can mimic blue naevus–like melanoma.

cards.title: Nodular melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Nodular melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis Unpigmented tumours must be distinguished from squamous cell carcinomas, appendageal tumours, sarcomas, and cutaneous lymphomas by immunohistochemistry. Melanoma metastases tend to have more mitoses or intravascular deposits of neoplastic melanocytes at the base.

Cytologically, the lesional cells are rather uniform and have atypical, hyperchromatic nuclei and abundant cytoplasm containing varying amounts of melanin that often consists of small, “dusty” particles. This “uniform cytological atypia” is of considerable diagnostic importance and contrasts with the random atypia of dysplastic nevi. cards.title: Invasive melanoma — ICD-10: C43 - malignant melanoma of skin
cards.excerpt:
Epidemiology
Incidence: 3.2 age standardized rate (world) (CA Cancer J Clin 2021;71:209)
~1.7% of global cancer (CA Cancer J Clin 2021;71:209)
Incidence has risen rapidly over the last 50 years (J Invest Dermatol 2009;129:1666)
Higher incidence in periequatorial zone (CA Cancer J Clin 2021;71:209)
M:F = 1.5:1 (SEER: Cancer Stat Facts - Melanoma of the Skin [Accessed 24 July 2025])

cards.title: Invasive melanoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Multistep process that involves interaction of genomic, environmental and host factors
4 step model proposed (Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 2016;29:122)
Mitogenic driver mutation (i.e., BRAF mutation)
Escaping primary senescence (i.e., CDKN2A loss)
Overcoming apoptosis (i.e., TP53 mutation)
Immortalization (i.e., TERTp mutation)

who_cross_mentions.snippet: Entity: Nodular melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis Unpigmented tumours must be distinguished from squamous cell carcinomas, appendageal tumours, sarcomas, and cutaneous lymphomas by immunohistochemistry. Melanoma metastases tend to have more mitoses or intravascular deposits of neoplastic melanocytes at the base.

missing_essentials: The draft omits that dermal melanophages and a dense, bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate are usually present in invasive lesions (Derm Levers, page 180).

The draft does not mention that identification of an intradermal or subcutaneous nodule of malignant neoplastic melanocytes is essential in metastatic melanoma (WHO Melanoma metastatic to the skin), but since this overlaps with metastatic rather than invasive primary, not essential to include.

In the Ancillary Tests section, the draft does not specify that in challenging cases of diagnosis, molecular confirmation is desirable (from WHO Melanoma metastatic to the skin, ancillary diagnostic criteria), though this is borderline since it refers to metastasis.

The draft omits that neoplastic melanocytes in dermal melanoma express melanocytic markers including melan-A, SOX10, HMB45, and S100 (WHO Dermal melanoma, ancillary studies; this could strengthen the Ancillary Tests section).
confusing: Under Differential Diagnosis, the bullet for 'Halo nevus with lichenoid inflammation' is confusing by combining secondary/adjacent melanoma criteria with the DDx description; criteria for melanoma vs. halo nevus might be more clearly partitioned.
entity_conflation: The draft incorporates findings from metastatic melanoma (e.g., 'history of melanoma; immunohistochemical and/or molecular confirmation in challenging cases; cytological ... features similar to those of primary melanoma') without clarifying that these pertain to metastatic not primary invasive melanoma.
missing_ddx_entities: Dysplastic nevus with florid fibroplasia (WHO Recurrent nevus DDx)
figure_issues: The draft includes a limited selection of figures and should ideally link/label or indicate a representative range e.g., Lentigo maligna melanoma, acral lentiginous melanoma, and other provided subtypes, which are present in evidence figures.
critic_json.notes_for_revision: Add mention of the classic stromal/dermal findings (dermal melanophages, dense bandlike lymphoid infiltrate) from Levers and mention that expression of melan-A, SOX10, S100, HMB45 in dermal melanomas is typical. Clarify when features relate to metastatic disease versus primary invasive melanoma to avoid entity conflation. Consider restructuring the Halo nevus DDx bullet for clarity and add missing DDx of sclerosing naevus and dysplastic nevus with florid fibroplasia. Expand figure usage to ensure representative coverage of major melanoma subtypes.
